Gusto’s cross from the right is put behind by Konsa for a Chelsea corner out on the right. Neto clips it in but Arsenal head away. James then opts to shoot from range and his effort is blocked by Gabriel. That shot looked to be going on target but Raya may have had it covered anyway.

Rice’s corner from the left is flicked on by Havertz at the near post and the last touch comes off James for another Arsenal corner on the other side. Arsenal take it short and fell to get into the danger zone but do win themselves another corner.

Saka delivers it into a dangerous area and the ball is flicked, looking like it is going into the Chelsea net, but Martinez makes the save whilst on the ground.

Havertz plays a first-time flick into the path of Saka, whose first-time effort looking for the far corner is saved well by Martinez to his right.

Odegaard feeds a clever pass into the Chelsea penalty area to pick out Zubimendi, whose shot is blocked.

Double change for Arsenal as Zubimendi and Hincapie replace Lewis-Skelly and Calafiori.

Palmer gets a shot away from the right side of the box but it is straight at Raya. Chelsea are just starting to wrestle back some momentum.

Gusto has only just come on but has a chance. The ball is laid to him on the edge of the box and he hits it first time but his effort goes over the bar.

The momentum is certainly with Arsenal right now so Xabi Alonso is making a double change. Gusto and Chavarria replace Lavia and Hato. With Gusto coming on for Lavia, Chelsea do not actually have any out-and-out central midfielders on the pitch.

Tzolis is the first Arsenal player into the book today. He is brought down by Lacroix and then demands that the Chelsea defender be booked, waving an imaginary card, and is then shown a yellow himself. Lacroix was also booked for the original foul.

Two former teammates challenge each other as Konsa slides in to make a perfectly-timed challenge on Rogers. The home crowd loved that tackle from Konsa, who won that tackle fair and square.

Chelsea made Odegaard angry about two minutes before that goal. The Arsenal captain, who is a mild-mannered guy, was really unhappy with a tackle by James. They were exchanging some verbals afterwards, before Odegaard then ran away from James to score.

That’s five goals Chelsea have conceded in just over a game-and-a-half since Emi Martinez took over in goal. In fairness, that Odegaard goal wasn’t his fault.

Arsenal were forced to respond when Chelsea scored early but now it is on the visitors to see how they respond after falling behind.

For the first time this afternoon, Arsenal lead and it is a quality goal. Tzolis receives it out on the left and cuts inside onto his right. Bukayo Saka has arrived at a career crossroads. We will soon learn whether he is destined to be a good Arsenal player or if he will elevate himself to the level of Premier League, Champions League and England great.

This weekend Saka turns 25, an age when footballers typically enter their peak. Although his legendary status at Arsenal is secure as a title winner, the reaction to the champions’ transfer window suggests there is a general feeling that he can and should produce more to earn “world class” status.

Mikel Arteta is short of such an attacker. He spent the summer investigating whether players of Vinícius Júnior and Julián Alvarez’s calibre might add much-needed stardust to his front three. It is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

It is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

“This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once said of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. But you know how you always push your ‘little friends’ at that age? Well, we tried, but he was a competitive monster.”

A personal opinion that no one asked for: Arsenal should have signed Joao Pedro last summer, when the Brazilian joined Chelsea for £60m. Arsenal bought Viktor Gyokeres instead, in a deal that could ultimately be more expensive, and there is no doubt which forward offers more to their team. Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

The departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

“We are better equipped,” said Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very important to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”

Chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso said. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, big and small.

“We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of big personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.

"The game will come down to mentality after a tough game on Saturday," said Huddersfield coach Drury. "They had a tough game on Saturday.

"We played Peterborough recently and we knew how chaotic that game was and how much it takes out of you physically and mentally.

"We had a tough derby game on Saturday, so I often feel Tuesdays, as much as there's some tactical elements to it, a lot of it will come down to mentality.

"I think what both teams do without the ball will be key. As much as both teams have got many good footballers and can do things with the ball, it'll come down to the other side of the game in my own instinct.

"It's a different challenge, a completely different style of football.

"They can play in a variety of ways. They're not just set in a certain way.

"They've got a really, really good side and it's been a really good moment in terms of form. I think Jack's done a brilliant job there.

#1900. 'Lucky': Arsenal get double referee verdict over Noni Madueke and Jurrien Timber incidents

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal have been told that Jurrien Timber was “lucky” to not concede a penalty in Sunday’s win over Liverpool, while Alexis Mac Allister has been labelled “embarrassing” for his clash with Noni Madueke.

The Dutchman pulled the shirt of Alexander Isak as the Liverpool striker attempted to get on the end of a cross, though Isak did not go to ground despite that contact preventing him getting to the ball.

Referee Andy Madley waved away Liverpool’s appeals and VAR did not intervene to overrule that decision.

Andoni Iraola was left bemused by the incident and revealed he will now have a very clear message for his players in the opposition’s box.

He said: "The answer is you have to dive, if you don't dive they won't call it."

Looking back on the pull from Timber, former referee Dermot Gallagher suggested that the error was from the officials on the pitch rather than VAR, as he indicated a penalty should have been awarded.

"It depends which angle you watch it from,” Gallagher told Sky Sports.

“The first angle, you see nothing. That is the referee's angle. The second angle, which is what VAR looks at, and it is a lot more damning.

"VAR looks at it in slow motion, which is another thing against him. In normal speed, he grabs and grabs him quickly but let's go. Does he do enough [for a penalty]?

"What is Timber's intention? He is on the wrong side of him. Does he do enough to stop him? He [Isak] will say yes, as he is close to the ball.

"VAR would be accused of re-refereeing if it is a penalty. It is a case of damned if they do and damned if they don't.

"It has to be the case of on-field. The more I watch it, the more I think he [Timber] has taken a big chance and has got lucky."

Tim Sherwood added: "I can't see where the ref is. It is a penalty. It is a nailed-on penalty.

"We have VAR to help the referee out, surely they have to help him out there. That is not re-refereeing the game.”

There were several flashpoints in the match, as Arsenal won at Anfield in the Premier League for the first time since 2012.

In the second half, Mac Allister went down holding his face, claiming that he had been headbutted by Madueke.

Jay Bothroyd described that as “embarrassing”.

“I tell you what I think it is, it's embarrassing from Mac Allister,” Bothroyd said.

“He looks like he has taken a full blown headbutt to the nose. When he has his hands [over his face] and takes them away, I am expecting to see a nose all over the place and blood coming out of his face.

"He goes down and it's like, what are you doing? You're a grown man. I hate it when I see those sort of things in a game."

Gallagher indicated that Mac Allister came close to getting a red card himself for a stamp tackle on Ezri Konsa, where he got the ball but took a risk with the manner of the challenge.

"It is two-footed, but he gets to the ball and doesn't get the man,” Gallagher said.

"If he got the man, he is in big trouble. You can't tackle like that."

Both teams had chances to score after Havertz’s opener but the game finished 1-0 as Arsenal moved three points clear at the top of the Premier League and Liverpool failed to climb back into the Champions League spots.

Rice was named Player of the Match after Arsenal’s battling victory and Carragher agreed with that decision, hailing him as not only the best midfielder in the Premier League but one of the greatest in the club’s history.

Manchester United could be sweating over the fitness of Leny Yoro ahead of their Champions League clash with Roma.

The Red Devils welcome the Serie A side to Old Trafford on Tuesday as Michael Carrick looks to put a stop to his side’s nine-match winless run.

The under-fire head coach has seen pressure mount on his shoulders, and particularly after three straight defeats.

United were thrashed 4-1 and 3-0 by Como and Bournemouth respectively a fortnight ago, and a 2-0 loss at Chelsea followed last weekend, as Lisandro Martinez was sent off at Stamford Bridge and Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer got the goals to hand Xabi Alonso’s hosts all three points.

Now, attentions turn back to the continent, where United sit 20th after three games.

The Dane had been sidelined with a hamstring problem that he picked up on international duty in September, but his comeback will be hugely welcomed amid United’s lack of senior left-back options.

However, there was cause for concern as eagle-eyed fans spotted defender Yoro strapped up ahead of Tuesday’s game.

The Frenchman, who has filled in at right-back to accommodate for Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui’s shift to left-back, was once again fielded at full-back in west London over the weekend, where he played the full 90 minutes.

He was seen with strapping on his knee while training, but did not look in discomfort as he participated in various drills.

The Frenchman could well be reinstated at centre-back should Carrick look to rotate his defensive unit, with Martinez suspended for the upcoming Premier League clash against Aston Villa.

Alexis Mac Allister’s attempts to get Noni Madueke sent off during Liverpool’s defeat to Arsenal have been branded a ‘joke’ and ’embarrassing’ by Reds legend Jamie Carragher.

Kai Havertz scored the only goal of the game at Anfield as the Gunners moved to the top of the Premier League table and Liverpool stayed fifth.

Andoni Iraola’s team had more possession, xG and shots than the visitors, but did not get a single one of their efforts on target.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard went down after a challenge with the Argentine, with Mac Allister then shouting something at the felled Norwegian before slapping him on the back of the head.

Jurrien Timber took umbrage with that and Madueke then got involved, squaring up to the Liverpool star and as their heads briefly met, Mac Allister went down holding his forehead.

Clearly it was an attempt to get the Gunners winger sent off, but neither the referee nor VAR were buying it and Madueke avoided any punishment.

Carragher made his feelings very clear on Mac Allister’s action, calling the World Cup winner ’embarrassing’ for his ‘joke’ of a response to the coming together.

‘I think everybody in the country watching football this head-to-head stuff. If someone puts their head back and butts, or course red card, but this stuff about head-to-head and if someone touches, the other one goes down and the payer gets sent off.

#1889. Aston Villa make legal action decision after Jamie Carragher apology

Aston Villa have decided against taking legal action against Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher.

The club had threatened legal proceedings against the former England defender after he made "unacceptable insults" on the Stick To Football podcast last week.

Carragher told Villa supporters to "shut the f*** up" after facing criticism for suggesting Unai Emery should consider taking the Manchester United job if Michael Carrick is sacked.

The pundit apologised on social media, admitting his language was "clumsy and wrong".

Villa will take no further action, the Press Association reports.

"Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football."

Carragher quickly apologised, insisting his comments were "tongue in cheek".

He posted on social media: "I’d like to apologise to Aston Villa, the owners and their fans.

"My language this week was clumsy and wrong.

Villa return to Champions League action on Tuesday when they take on Barcelona at the Nou Camp.

#1887. Monza 0-5 Milan Primavera: Zaramella shines in much-needed trashing

After a tough run in the league, Milan Primavera managed to build on their mid-week cup win with a strong performance against Monza this afternoon.

Excluding Wednesday’s win against Catanzaro in the Primavera Cup, Milan Primavera had lost four of their last five games heading into today’s clash. In short, a response was needed in the league as well and that is exactly what Giovanni Renna got.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There is still a long way to go, especially when you consider how much Monza have struggled so far, but it’s a crucial confidence boost to build on.

Milan Primavera opened the scoring in the 24th minute through Max Anastasio. The winger received the ball on the left flank and cut inside to shoot with his right foot. He managed to beat the goalkeeper with a nice strike, giving his side a perfect start.

It didn’t take long before the second goal arrived: four minutes later, Francesco Domnitei fired a shot on target and forced the goalkeeper to a save. However, he couldn’t control the rebound, which Mattia Zaramella pounced on for an easy goal.

Before the first half was up, Luca Nolli almost made it 3-0, hitting the post with an effort from close range. Either way, it was a great first half that put the Rossoneri in a very difficult position.

Zaramella picked out Riccardo Grassini in the box after winning the ball back high up the pitch, and the latter didn’t make any mistakes with the finish. Five minutes later, similarly to the first and second goals, Zaramella got his brace after picking up a good position inside the box.

It didn’t end there as Yanis Messaoudi made the most of a corner in the dying minutes, finding the back of the net with a header. 5-0, in other words, and a huge win for Milan Primavera to move to eight place at the time of writing.

#1883. Huddersfield Town v Luton Town: Radinio Balker on 2026-27 Terriers spirit

Saturday's 3-0 win at Bradford City was one of the rare occasions this season coach Martin Drury has left a fit player out of a winning team, but Dutch centre-back Balker justified his return, and will be hoping to hold onto his place at home to Luton Town on Tuesday.

If he does not, there will be no hard flings.

"If you're a team, you also need to cheer when someone else in your position is doing well," says Balker. "I tried to do that last season when I wasn't playing.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"We have 46 games plus cup games, so altogether probably 58 to 60. I won't be able to play 60 games, unfortunately.

"But if we have capable players in the same area at the same kind of level, then it's always good for the team because everybody profits from a team-mate being good and also going up in leagues.

An adductor injury to Balker opened the door to Joe Low to make his first League One start of the season at Plymouth Argyle and he did so well defensively that Balker returned alongside rather than instead of him. But on top of that, Low scored a spectacular overhead kick at Valley Parade on Saturday.

"I'm just really happy for him because it hasn't been the easiest for him the first few months," grins Balker. "Last season he was starting most of the games and then this season not starting from the beginning is quite difficult.

"I always said to him to keep working hard. I was in a similar situation last season where I wasn't playing in the beginning but I kept working hard. I told him to do the same.

"If you look at what he's done the last four games, it's been amazing. And then to score a goal like that, that's amazing."

To see the smile on the 28-year-old's face makes you believe it is more than just a professional footballer trotting out the lines he thinks he ought to.

It is a selflessness Drury made his top priority in his first summer as coach, when Balker received a one-year contract extension – "a show of faith," he says – despite being unable to consistently show his best form over two injury-hit seasons.

"It was top of the list," says Drury when asked how important that mindset was in assembling this season's squad.

"If you want to build a culture, it's not about the footballer, it's about the man. It's about the human being.

"Alongside that is being available to play. They're the first two, and then we'll look at things after that in terms of their qualities and what they can bring to us as footballers."

Being a good team-mate is something Balker is conscious of.

"It's very easy if everything is going well," he admits.

"When you're injured or when you come from a different team and you're not starting, it's very easy to forget about those players, but they are just as important.

"I've been there myself so that's why I try to help where I can.

"I wouldn't say last season or the season before was bad, necessarily, but this season there's a different camaraderie, I would say.

"Maybe the wins help, I don't know, but definitely at the moment, I think it feels like everybody wants to fight for each other.

"People are allowed to show that they're not happy as long as it's not affecting the thing they have to do on the ball."

With four wins out of four – the same as Huddersfield - Luton will test the table-toppers' Terrier spirit on Tuesday – and in a very different way to how Bradford tried to.

"They've been in a good form, just like us," says Balker. "Even last season, even though they weren't at their best they played really good football, difficult to play against.

"It's going to be a good game. We have to win because we're at home and we're confident we can do that.

"We all know that there are different styles of football (between Bradford and Luton).

"I think this season the big difference is that we're not really changing a lot in the sense of how we approach a game. We don't have to change formation or we don't have to change how we press.

"We have certain ways that we have to press that you don't have to think about. That really helps for us to be okay with changing from a bit more direct to a bit more football."

Whatever Huddersfield face on Tuesday, they will face it together.

"You need a new group of men that are humble, that are selfless, that are willing to work," says Drury. "I think the (coaching) staff sense right now that all the players are quite enjoying spending time together, both on and off the pitch.

"But look, it's really early days. Let's see if they enjoy each other's company in a couple of months' time, when we're in the midst of December and January."

At times in a tough few years for Town, that spirit has buckled. It will not if everyone thinks like Balker.

#1882. Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

As Dominic says, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

Free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

Bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

George has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

“He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

Johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh

We hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

Both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

Brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite launched himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

Fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

Now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Big shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire returns to the fray as Everton pass the ball through midfield to Johnson on the right. His cross, aiming for Barry, is cut out by Maguire and cleared to halfway. Back come Everton until Dewsbury-Hall is too rough with Mainoo as the Man Utd midfielder tackled him. Free-kick.

Lammens kicks the ball the full length of the field and Pickford picks it up. Mbeumo momentarily is at right-back with Dalot at centre-half.

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Big cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

We’re looking forward to seeing what [Brennan Johnson] does. We know he is very capable [and shown it] in recent seasons. Let’s hope he can bring us goals and assists as he did for Tottenham.

We’ve needed them [the two deadline day signings]. Maitland-Niles is physically fine. I don’t think Jack should be yet. We’ve needed it.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

No surprise United remain unchanged from the 5-2 win over Ipswich although Carrick will be looking for his side to score first here and make life a little easier for themselves after going behind to Hull and Ipswich in their opening two games. Brennan Johnson comes in for the departed Iliman Ndiaye, who joined Manchester City for £65m on deadline day. Jack Grealish is on the bench for Everton.

Moyes issued a call to arms to Everton fans in his programme notes after a dismal transfer window that has left him with just 18 outfield players. The Everton manager warning there may be difficult times to come.

“Finally, I must stress the importance of us all pulling together,” Moyes wrote.

“We need to be strong again and there may be occasions when we may have to find a way to get through some difficult moments.

“It is something you have all done in recent seasons. Everyone has pulled together for the good of the football club and we may need to do so again.”

We did a lot of good things [against Ipswich]. No two games are ever the same. We have different challenges today. We have to be ready for that with some slightly different ideas. But the boys did well last week, trained well this week and we’re really looking forward to it.

The next result is always the most important one regardless of what’s happened. Building momentum, building a run, of course it’s important. It’s game-by-game, as you know, but this is as tough as it comes for us, Everton away.

It’s not a major deal, we’ve got the squad and we can cope with it [increase in numbers of fixtures with the return to European football].

Everton  Pickford; Röhl, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry. Substitutes Travers, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Grealish, O’Brien, Dibling, Alcaraz, Hackney, Graham.

Man Utd  Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martínez, Shaw; Tielemans, Mainoo; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford; Cunha. Substitutes Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko.

"Whatever's gone on over the last few days is nothing to do with us as players" James Tarkowski is hoping Everton can get three points against Manchester United 🔵Watch Super Sunday live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/PMWBO5Oiah

🔴 The Reds are unchanged from last week's win over Ipswich 👊

Mason Mount is fit enough for the bench and takes Shea Lacey’s seat

Brennan Johnson comes in for Iliman Ndiaye, now at Man City. Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Jack Grealish start on the bench.

Today's Toffees to face @ManUtd. COYB! 🔵#EVEMUN pic.twitter.com/8s2UrcwR59

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

#1881. Michael Carrick reveals Manchester United injury latest as Patrick Dorgu makes surprise return

Michael Carrick has confirmed that Patrick Dorgu will not feature for Manchester United against Roma.

The winger returned to team training after an extended lay-off with a hamstring injury that he picked up on international duty in September.

It left the Red Devils without one of their senior left-back options, and that has led them to be short in that position after Luke Shaw’s muscle injury which has also kept the England international out.

Dorgu’s comeback is a big boost to under-fire head coach Carrick, who has overseen a nine-game winless run which has piled on the pressure on the former midfielder.

However, the Dane will not play any part as United return to continental competition tomorrow.

"It was his first day with the group, great to have him back, but he won't be involved tomorrow,” Carrick told the media. “We'll see how he progresses for the week [ahead]."

The sack looked as though it was looming after 4-1 and 3-0 thrashings by Como and Bournemouth respectively, but he was retained by the club’s hierarchy ahead of the trip to Chelsea last weeknend.

United were beaten once more by the Blues, with Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer scoring for the hosts as Lisandro Martinez was sent off for the visitors, who slid to 17th in the Premier League table.

Carrick was also asked about Martinez’s mindset after the Argentine’s red card, which followed on from his stunning TV interview in the wake of the defeat by Atletico Madrid last month.

“I've got no concerns about commitment at all,” the head coach continued.

“Things happen in football, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you, but commitment is not an issue, for sure."

#1880. Peter Schmeichel makes bold title claim after Arsenal beat Liverpool

Peter Schmeichel says he remains unconvinced that any team in the Premier League is capable of seriously challenging Arsenal following the side’s 1-0 victory over Liverpool.

Kai Havertz scored the only goal of the game on Merseyside to ensure Arsenal moved three points clear at the top of the table following Manchester City’s slip-up against high-flying Brighton.

The Gunners were also beaten by the Seagulls in September but have roared back emphatically in their last four matches, claiming maximum points and conceding just one goal in that time.

Sunday’s resilient win over Liverpool was their first at Anfield since as far back as 2012 and Mikel Arteta’s men will look to pick up where they left off when they return to top-flight action at home to Hull next weekend.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The reigning English champions have a midweek trip to Slavia Prague to contend with first, though, and Arteta will no doubt be desperate for his squad to return to from the Czech Republic unscathed.

Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool enjoyed over 56 per cent of the possession against Arsenal and took 17 shots on goal compared to the visitors’ ten, although not one of those efforts was on target.

But Arsenal came on top with the one statistic that truly mattered in a spirited performance that left Manchester United legend Schmeichel even more confident that the north Londoners would defend their title.

‘That performance, to come here to Anfield and win 1-0, I don’t care about the manner,’ he said on Viaplay.

‘We can discuss that and we’ve done that for two years now.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Now they are winners and I can’t see anyone, with that squad and what he has available to him, Arteta, who can challenge this team.’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Schmeichel reserved special praise for Noni Madueke and credited Arteta with helping to turn the winger from just a ‘talent’ into a ‘fantastic football player’.

‘Remember when he was at Chelsea, we sat there right behind the bench, he got substituted in one of the games we covered,’ the Dane said of Madueke.

‘We all spoke about his behaviour afterwards… you never become a great player when you behave like that.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Now, what we’ve just seen in the game [against Liverpool], it’s great manager work.

‘He’s produced a fantastic football player out of a great talent that we always thought was just going to be a talent.’

Ex-Arsenal winger Freddie Ljungberg was similarly glowing with his praise for Madueke and backed the England international to play a ‘very important’ role for the club over the coming months.

‘He’s a top talent,’ Ljungberg, a member of Arsene Wenger’s Invincibles squad, explained.

‘He’s different to Bukayo [Saka]. Bukayo is more of a solid player, would you call it that? He stands and makes the right decisions, angles, shots, knows what he’s doing.

‘Madueke is a bit more: one against one and I’m going. Rapid, more direct and sometimes we criticise him, maybe, for his defensive effort. Is he at the right angle? Is he protecting the centre? What is he doing defensively? And he switches off.

‘But he did not do that against Liverpool. It was a very mature performance from him because that’s what we sometimes say, “Don’t switch off!”, and he didn’t.

‘He did really well and he’s going to be very important.’

#1879. Cardinale urges Milan fans to ‘come together’ to win: “It has to be everybody”

Yesterday evening, Gerry Cardinale was stopped by Carlo Pellegatti for an impromptu interview and he urged the AC Milan fans to ‘come together’.

Between the two defeats in the Europa League and the three draws in the league, it has been a so-so start to the season for Milan. In that sense, tonight’s derby against Inter could act as a catalyst for a good period, as a win would take them within four points of the Nerazzurri.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim knows it and the players know it, so it will be very interesting to see if we will get a good response tonight or another disappointing performance. The pressure is certainly on, even if the support from the fans will be amazing too.

Speaking to Carlo Pellegatti last night in what was an impromptu interview, Cardinale urged the Milan fans to ‘come together’ as winning isn’t just about the players performing well. It needs to be a perfect ecosystem in which everyone plays their part.

“Listen, we have to come together. If we want to win, it has to be everybody. The fans, us, the press, anybody who supports AC Milan. Let’s come together and all make this possible. Ruben is doing a great job, I made the right decision on Ruben.

“I watched him today at Milanello and he really cares about his training, his managing, his coaching, and his mentoring. I met with every single one of our players and they want to win. It’s only a matter of time.

“You either want to win or you don’t want to win. You can’t fake that. I want to win, the players want to win and Amorim wants to win. I’m telling you, that I got right. Now, football is up and down, but I promise you that they want to win,” he stated.

#1878. Dave Challinor spoilt for choice as he looks for Sheffield Wednesday's golden blend

The principles Challinor, pictured, wants to see in blue-and-white stripes will have been hammered home on day one, putting into action the promises he will have made in a job interview which, given why Henrik Pedersen was sacked, will almost certainly have centred around front-footed, attacking football.

But when it comes to the formation, he almost has too much to choose from.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Luckily for him, his first two matches are in cup football and his third is likely to be postponed due to international call-ups. Not until the November 20 derby at Barnsley will he have to show his hand.

Of course his decision could be to not have a fixed formation at all. Some teams benefit from having a set shape, particularly those nearer the top of the table who aspire to dictate terms. But Challinor's Stockport County flitted between three and four at the back last season.

The task is always getting as many of your best players on the field in a way that makes the most of as many of them as possible.

Although it did not garner the win Challinor would have wanted as he watched from the Hillsborough stands, Matt Hamshaw's final – at least for now – match as caretaker manager showcased the team in a back three and a four, albeit a 4-4-1, after Sil Swinkels was sent off in the first half.

But the starting 3-4-2-1 will have given food for thought, with Callum Slattery, Davis Keillor-Dunn and Mason Burstow linking well with Jamal Lowe banned, Louie Barry injured, and Harry Gray, Keiran Morrison and Jordi Liongola benched.

“I was looking to see how I could get two up front and work backwards from there,” said Hamshaw. “It's just about finding a way to win.”

Despite Lowe's productive start to the campaign, centre-forward does not look the strong point of this squad. Keillor-Dunn can play as one but he too is a free spirit, better in the hole or at last as one of a pair. Slattery and Gray are best not tied to the wings.

The Owls also have plenty of solid centre-halves. Even with Liam Cooper and Di'Shon Bernard injured, they were still able to field Swinkels, Liam Palmer and Ernie Weaver, and have Gabriel Otegbayo on the bench.

Three at the back also makes it easy to get Max Lowe and Reece James – when fit again in four to six weeks' time – in the same side.

Giving Yan Valery freedom as a wing-back should get the best out of him too.

But by the same token, a fit Barry and Liverpool loanee Morrison are two of the better players, and most effective wide. Morrison is young and still erratic but a proper winger; the absence of wide attacker Barry seems to have hit the squad harder than it ought to have.

So perhaps a 4-2-3-1 or a 4-4-2 is in order.

Ultimately what did for Pedersen was the sense that he was not getting the best out of some talented ingredients. Finding the right mix is Challinor's challenge.

#1877. Man Utd need a Mikel Arteta in charge - but club's rotten core means any manager is a dead man walking

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

There are a couple of signs that a Premier League manager at one of the traditional top clubs is fearing for his job.

One, obviously, is an extended poor run of results. The second is the 'Mikel Arteta Got Time And Look At Arsenal Now' card gets whipped out. It has never been played from a position of strength.

The idea that Arteta's tenure at Arsenal is something of a blueprint has been regularly latched onto by those at rival clubs, the suggestion being that time and time alone is the answer to all problems.

When his time in the Tottenham dugout was stumbling to an early conclusion, Thomas Frank pointed hopefully across north London.

“I think it is a good example of a club that sticks to the process," Frank said.

“It took probably three seasons for Arteta, so the fourth season, that is where he competed. Now he is in the seventh season. So he is really, really ready to compete in his fourth season."

There was nothing in Frank's tenure to suggest he deserved to make it that far. No bold, ambitious thinking. No long-term vision to persuade supporters or the club's hierarchy that short-term pain was worth enduring.

His authority was consistently eroded. Frank disciplined Yves Bissouma, a player already heading for the exit door, for lateness, but dissent from Cristian Romero, Djed Spence and Micky van de Ven all later went unpunished.

Michael Carrick is the latest to use Arteta as something of a shield in an attempt to cling onto his Manchester United job, despite the best efforts of his players.

"It pains me to say, but the one that won the league in our country last season has been there for a long period of time," Carrick said last month.

"It’s seven years, and the first two seasons [they finished] maybe eighth or seventh."

Whether they were given seven months, seven years, or seven decades, most managers would not have turned around the mess that Arsenal were in when Arteta took charge.

Carrick reveals Man Utd injury latest after surprise return

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal eye Brazil star; Man Utd in Barcelona swap

Gravenberch angers Liverpool fans with Timber interaction

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

The desperation for results is prioritised over addressing Manchester United’s rotten core

The Spaniard possesses a unique character, an aura that brings people along with him. It was that intensity and force of character that persuaded Arsenal to take a punt on him. Within a year, he was promoted from head coach to manager. What has followed since is testament to the extraordinary leader he is.

Crucially, Arteta had people above him willing to go all in. He wanted decisive action and Arsenal backed him.

Henrikh Mkhitaryan had his contract terminated barely six months into Arteta’s reign. Mesut Ozil, the club's highest-paid player, was cast aside and had his deal torn up in the Spaniard’s first full season in charge. Sokratis and Shkodran Mustafi followed almost immediately in similarly ruthless exits.

Arsenal needed a cultural reset. Arteta had the personality to demand that but also the authority to enact it. Club captain Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang was stripped of his duties for repeatedly being late and ultimately had his contract ripped up as well.

The impact? Mohammed Elneny said in 2022: "Everyone is scared with their position because this happened to Aubameyang.

"Of course if anyone is not the captain of the team, does a small mistake, they are going to have the same problem, and no one needs that problem."

Arsenal's hierarchy could very easily have sided with Aubameyang or Ozil, both on £350,000-a-week, over Arteta. That would have been less embarrassing from an optics and a financial perspective. Instead, a line was drawn in the sand.

Player power would not usurp Arteta's authority. Everything since then, from the harmonious dressing room to the connection with the fans, from the extraordinary work-rate of his players to the pride in defending the cause, has been built on those foundations.

Time will not help Carrick at United when he has been given no other tools. Lisandro Martinez, who should have been moved on a long time ago, slagged off the club's executives but was not dropped. Two matches later, he displayed remarkable stupidity in being sent off against Chelsea.

Bruno Fernandes, the club captain, took aim at Carrick himself. He sat out for one match but then returned with the armband still in his possession. The desperation for results was prioritised over addressing the club's rotten core.

The same players will get another manager sacked. Results will pick up and optimism will briefly return, but the underlying issues will remain. Nothing fundamentally will have changed.

It is easy to throw out buzzwords like patience and process, just as it is easy to allow a manager to limp on towards an inevitable conclusion, hoping to hide from deeper failings and another major decision the hierarchy got wrong.

Clubs want to believe in the Arteta model without signing up to the pain that comes with it. That is a blueprint, but only for further decline.

#1876. Arsenal star says Alexis Mac Allister was ‘clever’ in controversial moment

Noni Madueke did not join in with the chorus of criticism aimed at Alexis Mac Allister after their clash at Anfield, saying the Liverpool star was ‘obviously clever’ during the incident.

Arsenal left Anfield with a 1-0 win thanks to a first-half Kai Havertz goal as they moved three points clear at the top of the Premier League table.

It was an entertaining contest, despite Liverpool not managing a shot on target, with a decent amount of edge to the game.

There was a flash point late in the match as Mac Allister appeared furious with a felled Martin Odegaard, shouting at the Norwegian and slapping him on the back of the head.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Jurrien Timber, in turn, was fuming with that response as he rushed to confront the Argentina international.

As the pair squared up, Madueke got involved and went head-to-head with Mac Allister, who then went down, claiming to have been headbutted.

He clearly had not been and neither the referee nor VAR were buying his theatrical attempt to get the Arsenal winger dismissed.

Jamie Carragher was extremely critical of Mac Allister for how he tried to engineer a red card for his opponent, but Madueke was more charitable, acknowledging that he was being baited, but it was ‘clever’ to do so.

‘To be honest, I don’t think it’s anything. Whether it’s a yellow or red card, the referee didn’t think that. VAR didn’t think that. So we all agreed there,’ Madueke told Viaplay.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘It’s a natural movement and he is obviously clever. He tried to bait me into getting a red card there.

‘In my head, I’ll be very honest with you guys, in my head I was thinking: “It’s possible, you know, with VAR”. It’s about whoever interprets it. I don’t know what they’re thinking. But thankfully it wasn’t.’

Liverpool legend Carragher went on a rant against players acting as Mac Allister did at Anfield, calling his reaction a ‘joke’ and calling for the sport to stamp it out.

‘I’m delighted he never got sent off there. We have got to be strong on calling people out and saying that this is embarrassing. I cant stand it,’ Carragher told Sky Sports.

‘I think everybody in the country watching football this head-to-head stuff. If someone puts their head back and butts, or course red card, but this stuff about head-to-head and if someone touches, the other one goes down and the payer gets sent off.

‘As a game, as football, people in the Premier League, supporters, call your own people out for it.

‘I’m a Liverpool fan, that’s a joke from Mac Allister but it’s got to stop. People are trying to gain an advantage because they know they can because red cards are getting given for it.

‘Whether it’s from Howard Webb, the Premier League, the managers get together. This has got to stop. Stop getting red cards for this crap!’

#1875. Alan Shearer makes Arsenal claim after win over Liverpool

Alan Shearer hailed Arsenal’s defence as the ‘best in world football’ after a hard-fought win over Liverpool.

The reigning champions moved to the top of the Premier League with a 1-0 victory at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

Kai Havertz gave Arsenal the lead on 16 minutes and that proved to be enough to bag all three points despite some intense Liverpool pressure.

While Liverpool mounted attack after attack, they mustered just one shot on target against an Arsenal side who have conceded just 10 goals in 15 games this season.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘That is how you work as a team,’ Shearer told Premier League Productions after Arsenal’s first win at Anfield in 14 years. ‘That is how you defend as a team.

‘Every single one of them to a man were outstanding. When they were under the cosh in the second half, you could see how much they wanted to defend and what it means to them to keep a clean sheet.

‘I don’t think there is a better team in world football that defend quite like Arsenal defend. Every player does their bit, it isn’t just the back four.

‘It was brilliant sitting behind the Arsenal bench today and seeing what it means to them. The team ethic and team work and belief Arteta has in them.

‘He didn’t get flustered at all even when Arsenal had to suffer. He trusts his players.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Former Arsenal winger Theo Walcott also heaped praise on the Gunners’ defence, insisting that solidity will make Mikel Arteta’s side ‘difficult to stop this year’.

‘Arsenal frustrated them,’ Walcott said. ‘To limit Liverpool to no shots on target shows the level of this team. They just love defending, don’t they?

‘I felt like they don’t mind that pressure. These are champions who can do a bit of everything. They are going to be difficult to stop this year.

‘I look at Arsenal’s forward players and at no point do they get frustrated working for the team. That is different to many years ago.

‘I remember the Arsenal teams I played in and we always wanted to attack. Now they are happy to work for the team.

‘To win championships, you have to keep clean sheets, and that starts from the front. There are no players switching off, or giving up.’

While Arsenal underlined their status as Premier League title favourites at Anfield, Liverpool suffered a humbling defeat after a promising run under Andoni Iraola.

Liverpool hero Steve McManaman said: ‘They were the better team today, but they’ve walked off losing with just one shot on target.

‘In the second half they had lots of possession, their effort and work rate and enthusiasm was all there. They were just missing that little bit of magic.’

Arsenal and Liverpool are both in Champions League action this week, with the Gunners facing Slavia Prague and the Reds visiting Fenerbahce.

#1873. Michael Carrick makes 'crazy' admission as Manchester United delay sack decision

Michael Carrick does not feel like his time as Manchester United manager is running out.

The under-fire head coach has overseen a run of nine straight games without a victory this term, and his United side sit 17th in the Premier League after their worst start to a campaign in 40 years.

The Red Devils have won just once in the league all season, with their other victory coming in the Champions League against minnows Sabah.

On the continent, they were handed hefty defeats by Atletico Madrid and Como, with the latter resulting in Carrick apologising to the travelling supporters, raising his hands in acknowledgement.

The writing seemed to be on the wall for the former midfielder after a heavy 3-0 demolition at home by Bournemouth, who ran riot at a tempestuous Old Trafford.

It seemed as though Carrick was waving goodbye to the United fans as he walked off the pitch, and the home faithful turned on the players with relentless booing at the full-time whistle as they trudged off.

United were beaten again last weekend as Chelsea secured a 2-0 win at Stamford Bridge, with Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer on the scoresheet for Xabi Alonso’s Blues.

Lisandro Martinez, who hit the headline for his open criticism of the club’s hierarchy following the loss at Atletico Madrid in October, was sent off in west London and Carrick did not acknowledge the centre-back as he made his way back to the dressing room.

Despite all that, Carrick does not feel like he is a “coach with two games left”, after it was reported that the club had spared him the sack, seeking to reassess his position during the November international break.

“You you never know what is going to happen in the future, but that doesn't change the way I feel. I can't wait for the agme tomorrow. You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had, but I can't wait for it."

United take on Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday before a home encounter with Aston Villa at the weekend.

#1872. Dwight Yorke names the manager Manchester United must appoint to replace Michael Carrick

Manchester United hero Dwight Yorke has told the Red Devils to pay whatever is necessary to bring in Unai Emery as manager.

Michael Carrick remains in charge at Old Trafford, but after nine games without a win his grip on the job looks very flimsy.

United have two games before the next international break, hosting Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday and then Emery’s Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday.

If they win neither of those contests then it seems extremely difficult to imagine Carrick will still be in charge when the players return from international duty.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Yorke, who played for Villa from 1989-98 before moving to Manchester United, says Emery is the only man for the job and the Red Devils should have done whatever they could to get him before they hired Ruben Amorim in 2024 and should do the same now.

‘I have said this all along, and it baffles me when people are now jumping on the bandwagon,’ Yorke said on talkSPORT.

‘I said this two-and-a-half years ago. Unai Emery was the man to go and get way before Amorim has come into the equation.

‘And just like how, you go and spend £70million on players, I think Unai Emery, you can go and spend that money, I am not saying £70m, but pay whatever Villa has asked and get him. Give him the authority to come in.

‘I have said that way before Amorim has come in. I got a backlash from the Villa fans, and to this day, I still believe that he is the best manager in the business, certainly to get Man Utd to some type of credibility and sustainability at the same time as well.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Yorke recognises that the Manchester United players are massively under-performing, but feels that Carrick has to take some of the blame for that as he appears unable to turn the tide.

‘When things are good, which it was really good under Carrick when he first took over, football is easy,’ said the former striker.

‘The difference in management is when things are not so good. As a player when things are not so good, have you got the character to bounce back?

‘This is where we have seen Carrick is being let down. You need a reaction from your players. Whether the players are on board with you, are they going to fight for you? I’ve not seen that.

‘We’ve seen Carrick in his element when things are really good. When things have not gone so well the manager’s job is trying to motivate the players, get them back to playing, showing some character, play with conviction, play with passion.

‘Even if you lose a football match, that’s fine. But if you lose football matches the way United have been losing football matches, I’m afraid that it does not look good.

‘You look at Tottenham, for instance, they were at the bottom and the manager somehow finds a way. You’ve got to find a way from your players and I’m not seeing that with Carrick.

‘This is the time as a manager when you’ve got to earn your coin and he’s not really doing that at the moment.’
