#1871. Manchester United XI vs Roma: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Champions League

Manchester United will not be able to welcome back Patrick Dorgu when they take on Roma this evening.

There had been a hope that the Dane could slot back in to solve the Red Devils’ left-back problems after the versatile winger returned to team training on Monday.

Michael Carrick, the under-fire head coach, confirmed to the media that while the former Lecce man had made a comeback, he would not be involved in the Champions League tie.

"It was his first day with the group, great to have him back, but he won't be involved tomorrow,” Carrick said. “We'll see how he progresses for the week [ahead]."

As such, it means that United are once again hamstrung in that position, with Luke Shaw also sidelined with a muscle problem.

Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui have deputised from right-back in recent matches, with central defender Leny Yoro coming in as a makeshift right-sided full-back. Ayden Heaven is also an option in that position.

Further forward, the Red Devils are still without Marcus Rashford, who remains sidelined with a niggling hip issue that kept him out of the heavy defeats by Como and Bournemouth, while he was not fit enough to face Chelsea either. He has not since returned to training, and will not feature here.

Benjamin Sesko is a longer-term absentee as the Slovenian continues his recovery from a shin problem that curtailed his debut campaign and stunted his start to this season.

It therefore leaves Carrick relatively short of options for the visit of Roma, but he will have Kobbie Mainoo to call upon in the engine room after the academy graduate returned to training ahead of the trip to Chelsea, and he was introduced as a substitute at Stamford Bridge.

The England international could well come into the starting lineup here, although it remains to be seen who could join him in centre-field.

Summer arrivals Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba have all been rotated in recent weeks as Carrick looks to experiment in a bid to save his job.

#1870. Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard says three teams can rival Arsenal for the Premier League title

Steven Gerrard believes Arsenal will retain the Premier League trophy but says three other teams will also ‘pull away’ at the top of the table.

The reigning champions reclaimed their position at the top of the Premier League with a hard-fought 1-0 win over Liverpool on Sunday.

Previous leaders Manchester City suffered another surprising defeat, losing 1-0 at home to Brighton, and Arsenal took full advantage with a narrow win at Anfield thanks to Kai Havertz’s first-half goal.

It was another performance from Arsenal that convinced Gerrard that the Premier League trophy will be heading back to the Emirates Stadium after Mikel Arteta ended the club’s 22-year wait last season.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

But Gerrard believes three other clubs – Man City, Liverpool and Chelsea – will also ‘pull away’ from their Premier League rivals and could all challenge Arsenal for the title.

‘Credit to Arsenal because that’s how you win leagues, going to places like Liverpool, being strong, sticking together, and putting in a different type of performance,’ Gerrard told The Overlap Daily, sponsored by Sky Bet.

‘It was full of grit and fight and togetherness, and they got over the line. And they will know that come the end of the season, if they win the league, which I think they will, I haven’t changed my mind from the beginning of the season, they will look back at that more than your four or five-nils where they look fantastic, because I’m sure they will at times.

‘They’ll look at that and think, we went to Anfield, tough crowd to play against, tough Liverpool performance, Andoni Iraola’s got this Liverpool team playing an awful lot better, Liverpool played well and we managed to get out of there with three points.

‘So it could be huge for Arsenal. At this moment in time, nine points behind for Liverpool. So, Liverpool have got work to do if they want to challenge.

‘But this Arsenal team just look as if they can beat teams in different ways. I think that could be the difference.’

‘I’m going to put my neck on the line and say that I think they will fall away from that, but that’s not a criticism, because I think they’re a top team with a top manager,’ Gerrard added.

‘I just think to go the distance over the course, I think the stronger teams in the league will pull away a bit, but I certainly think they’re top four contenders and the most dangerous team in the league at the moment to play, because they’re playing without fear.

‘Everyone knows their job in the team, in and out of possession. They’ve improved a lot, I would say, from a defensive point of view. And they’ve got so many dangerous players, people that are comfortable on the ball.

‘They’re fantastic to watch. I think Brighton are more of a threat for the top-four chasers because I think they’re going to push for Champions League places.

‘Over the course, you’re faced with so many different challenges in the Premier League. And I just think where Arsenal’s squad is, and City’s, the Liverpool squad, I just think over the course of the 38 games, the three teams, and Chelsea, when you look at Chelsea in the second half there, I think them teams will pull away a bit over the course.

‘But I think they’re going to push and I think they’re going to go for it and I’m really interested to see how hard they can push. They’re not a title contender, in my opinion.’

#1869. GdS: Why Milan and Inter are expected to bench their most in-form players

Alphadjo Cisse and Carlo Augusto are both expected to start on the bench in tonight’s Derby della Madonnina, despite being among the best players for AC Milan and Inter so far.

For Milan, tonight’s derby is a chance to extend their unbeaten run in the fixture and to decrease the gap in the standings. For Inter, it’s a chance to end the winless run and to truly assert themselves against the Rossoneri, with +10 in sight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In other words, it’s a very important game and the tactical battle is expected to play an important role in the outcome. Team selection is thus top of mind for Ruben Amorim and Cristian Chivu who, however, are looking to bench a couple of their best players: Cisse and Augusto.

Starting with Cisse, as Gazzetta dello Sport highlights, Amorim’s decision is both tactical and psychological. He fears that there will be too much pressure on the youngster’s shoulders, while the plan is also to play with a 4-4-1-1 that can turn into a 4-3-3 or a 4-2-3-1 depending on the moment.

In that sense, Amorim believes Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic are better suited to playing out wide than Cisse. More specifically, they arre better suited to playing out wide when not in possession, where Inter will push hard.

Playing with attacking-minded midfielders like Moreira and Pulisic, plus a trequartista like Cisse behind Goncalo Ramos (i.e. a 4-2-3-1), would result in an unbalanced team. Behind Ramos there will be Rabiot, who, when not in possession, will act as a central midfielder.

Therefore, Cisse will start on the bench and be used as needed in the second half.

Moving on to Augusto, over the past two months, he has saved Inter on numerous occasions: the assist that started the comeback against Napoli, the goal in Madrid, the turnaround goal against Bologna, and the decisive blow in the Champions League against Shakhtar.

The latest contribution was the own goal he forced against Venezia, which Chivu’s men used to seal a game that could have gone terribly wrong. Yet, in tonight’s derby against Milan, the Brazilian could start on the bench.

The battle with Federico Dimarco will be decided in the final hours, but the reality is that the Italian is still considered the starter on the left. As such, it’s a question of hierarchy, though we will likely see the player come off the bench either way.

#1867. Paul Merson slams Manchester United over Andrey Santos transfer and makes relegation claim

Paul Merson has criticised Manchester United’s decision to sign Andrey Santos and says the Red Devils will be in the relegation zone come December.

Brazilian midfielder Santos has made an inauspicious start to his United career following a £50m move from Chelsea over the summer.

The 22-year-old has started less than half of Manchester United’s games so far this season and struggled to make an impact when he has featured.

Santos is certainly not the only player at Old Trafford under-performing, with Michael Carrick’s side only out of the relegation zone on goal difference following their worst start to the season since the 1980s.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

United’s next five league games are against Aston Villa, Liverpool, Brentford, Newcastle United and Coventry City, and Merson believes they will be sitting in the drop zone by the time they face Frank Lampard’s side in early December.

‘Manchester United play Coventry on the 5th of December and I’d be shocked if they’re not in the bottom three by then,’ Merson told Sky Sports.

‘That’ll be about a third of the season gone then. They might go and get a big result next weekend, Aston Villa looked beatable the other day.

‘I don’t see them getting relegated, absolutely not. But this is not Manchester United and there’s no quick fix, they got it all wrong upstairs.

‘The first window, they went for the forward line but it wasn’t good enough. Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko, they’re nice players but they’re not 20-25 goal-a-season players.

Michael Carrick has delivered an update on Manchester United’s injury list ahead of his side’s clash with Roma.

The Red Devils return to European action on Tuesday as the Serie A side visit Old Trafford.

United are on a run of nine games without a victory in all competitions, which stretches back to the end of August, where they beat Ipswich Town 5-2.

That result is their only win in the Premier League to date, with their only other victory coming against minnows Sabah in the Champions League on matchday one.

The heat is cranking up on Carrick amid United’s poor run of form, which has seen three straight defeats, including heavy 4-1 and 3-0 results against Como and Bournemouth respectively.

Last time out, Carrick’s ten men - after Lisandro Martinez’s sending off - were beaten 2-0 by Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.

United have been dealing with persistent injuries so far this term, as they look to shake off their worst start to a season in 40 years.

They welcomed Kobbie Mainoo back off the bench at the weekend, while Patrick Dorgu returned to team training after a lay-off with a hamstring issue.

Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford have been sidelined with muscle and hips problems.

“It’s great to have him back," Carrick said of the returning Dorgu. "He's worked ever so hard to be back with the group, but he won’t be involved tomorrow.

"We’ll see how he progresses through the week.”

There was a concern as eagle-eyed fans spotted Leny Yoro sporting strapping on his knee in open training on Monday morning.

Carrick said of the Frenchman: "Leny has had a bit of a tendon [issue], it's one of them that comes and goes. But he's been fine and I've been delighted with him.”

As for Shaw and Rashford, neither of the England internationals will feature against Roma, with neither out training with their team-mates.

#1864. Derek McInnes admits Rangers were second best to Hearts as he endures difficult night on return to Tynecastle

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 19:56 EDT, 28 October 2026 | Updated: 20:24 EDT, 28 October 2026

Rangers boss Derek McInnes was left to lament basic defensive errors despite his team salvaging a point against Hearts on his return to Tynecastle.

McInnes’ side had taken a first-half lead through Kevin Kelsy, only to fall 2-1 behind after half-time when Claudio Braga and Calvin Miller struck for Hearts.

Rangers snatched a dramatic point at the death thanks to a header from Olwethu Makhanya, but it was a missed opportunity on a night when Celtic also dropped points.

McInnes, who was given a hostile reception as he went back to his old stomping ground in Gorgie and even appeared to become embroiled in an altercation with Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken at full-time, admitted that Rangers simply were not good enough to win on the night.

‘I think when you go in front at a place like this, we’re disappointed we never showed more authority in the game,’ he said.

‘I don’t think you expect to have control when you come to Tynecastle. We’ve got a very young forward line and I don’t think we secured the ball enough.

Wouter Vrancken and Derek McInnes share a frosty handshake at full-time at Tynecastle

‘I thought Hearts, certainly for that 15-minute period before half-time, kept picking up a lot of the ball and feeding their wider players and forward players.

‘I thought their forward players looked after the ball a lot better. We were giving away umpteen free-kicks and playing with fire, to be honest.

‘You’ve got to credit Hearts. I think they had the better players. I think they had three or four real top performers and players who played really well, I have to be honest with that.

‘We never started the second half. It’s inexplicable, really. We lose another free-kick, given away cheaply, and we get punished this time for it with Claudio’s goal.

‘They’re capable of punishing you and they were good enough to punish us. We never defended with any real certainty tonight and we needed to in those moments. Ultimately, we weren’t good enough to win the game.’

There seemed to be a bit of tension between McInnes and Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken at full-time but both managers brushed it off.

Hearts winger Calvin Miller had turned the game around when firing the Gorgie side ahead

‘I think he was just thanking me for how grateful he is for leaving him such a strong squad here,’ added McInnes.

Hearts boss Vrancken insisted he had nothing but praise for his team as they continue to battle through an injury crisis.

The Tynecastle side are without eight key players at present but gave a good account of themselves in what proved to be an entertaining encounter.

‘When you concede a goal so late, you’re always disappointed because I think we deserved the three points,’ he said.

‘It would have been a great win, but it was still a massive performance from us. I am really proud of what the players are doing at the moment.’

#1863. Pierre Sage makes sack admission as Crystal Palace future hangs in balance after Tottenham defeat

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Pierre Sage has called on Crystal Palace supporters to trust him, but admits his future is not in his hands after their 2-0 defeat to Tottenham.

Palace were comfortbaly beaten at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, with goals from Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke ensuring Spurs took advantage of Jean-Philippe Mateta’s early red card.

Sage is under increasing pressure to turn things around, with Palace mired in the relegation zone after winning one of their first nine league games, but he insists he will continue to fight for his future.

Asked if he was aware of the Eagles’ league position, Sage cut a defiant tone but added it was not up to him whether he kept his job.

“I am really aware of the situation,” Sage said.

“I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [my future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have ten years, I will give my best for ten years.”

Relegation fears are deepening for Palace, and Sage acknowledges that dropping down to the Championship would be a disaster for the club after their third successive defeat in the league.

"Yes, [relegation], it’s a disaster for every club in the Premier League and especially that I have to speak about my club. You know I’m not comfortable with the situation in the table, but it’s a consequence of what we did bad on the pitch,” the Frenchman continued.

“My only action is on the team and on the pitch. That is why I can speak about the situation of the club in the table, of my situation, because it’s a consequence to of this, but my only way to change a thing is to go on the pitch. That is why I talk to the players and I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. They can trust in me.

“I will never give up. I will do the best session I can do on Monday because now I have the rage to train more because the game I saw was not in line with my conviction.

“I don’t like when we let the initiative too much to the opponent. I was really impressed by what I see of the other team, and I like this kind of play. I know we are not the same team, but we are able to do things with the ball, and we have to improve that."

Arsenal fans believe that Piero Hincapie hit back at a subtle past dig from Virgil van Dijk following the club’s statement win over Liverpool.

#1861. Gasperini warns Roma not to be distracted by Man Utd’s struggles

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Gian Piero Gasperini has warned his Roma side not to be distracted by Manchester United's "difficult period" ahead of their Champions League encounter.

Roma head to Old Trafford with four points from their opening three league phase matches, drawing with Fenerbahce and defeating Slovan Bratislava either side of a dramatic defeat to Real Madrid.

Only Barcelona (65.4%) average more possession in the 2026-27 Champions League than Roma (61.3%), while only Bratislava (2026) and Feyenoord (1864) have allowed their opponents more passes in the competition this season than United (1781).

Michael Carrick's United have also struggled domestically this term, sitting 17th in the Premier League after losing to Chelsea at the weekend.

The Red Devils are winless in nine games across all competitions (D3 L6), but Gasperini is preparing to face "the best Manchester United".

"In the league they are going through a difficult period for results, but we can't let ourselves be distracted," Gasperini said.

Sunday morning training ahead of Manchester United  Thanks @Udinese_1896 for your hospitality  #ASRoma https://t.co/FaHfMPgHRH

— AS Roma English (@ASRomaEN) November 1, 2026

"United are still a strong team, they have players of absolute quality, and it's a hot, difficult environment. We are preparing as if we are facing the best Manchester United.

"Every situation is different. I don't know United's [situation] exactly, but I know they have strong players. You can suffer for a certain period, but then you manage to restart. Hopefully from the day after match!"

United and Roma have faced each other on eight occasions in Europe, with the Red Devils winning five of those (D1 L2).

The most recent meeting was won by Roma, however (3-2 in May 2021 in the Europa League).

Italian sides have faced United away from home in the European Cup/Champions League on 17 occasions, losing 13 of them (W3 D1).

The only three victories were all by a 1-0 scoreline: Juventus in 2018 and 1996, AC Milan in 2005.

Roma have only won two of their last 20 Champions League away games (D6 L12), while they have conceded in each of their last 32 on the road since a 2-0 win at Lyon in March 2007, the longest run without a clean sheet by any side away from home in European Cup history.

#1860. Photo: Curva Sud confirm banners and choreography will return for Milan-Inter

For Milan-Inter, we won’t just see the Curva Sud with full capacity for the first time since 2019, but also the return of several banners and a choreography.

The Derby della Madonnina is always a massive clash, but several factors will make tonight’s edition extra special. In addition to the league table element, with Milan chasing Inter, it will also be a fantastic one in the San Siro stands.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For the first time since 2019, the Curva Sud and Curva Nord won’t have a capped capacity, adding an additional 2,350 seats to what is usually available. You might have seen the covers before, the blue and green ones, but they won’t be there tonight.

In addition to the increased capacity, it will also be a Curva Sud in full swing on the choreography front. As confirmed by Curva Sud on their Instagram this afternoon, they will bring back some of the banners that they haven’t displayed as of late.

Of course, the banners that are still prohibited inside the stadium won’t be there, but at least there will be a lot more now. Furthermore, there will be a proper choreography at the start of the game, also known as a tifo.

In the last home derby, there was a tifo organised by the club itself, but not from Curva Sud. It will thus be very interesting to see what they have put together for this evening.

#1859. Arsenal player ratings vs Liverpool: 9/10 rock steps up in Anfield masterclass

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal went three points clear at the top of the Premier League table with a battling 1-0 win over Liverpool on Sunday.

Kai Havertz’s finish at the back post after a sweeping Arsenal move in the 16th minute proved to be the winner, as Arsenal came away from Anfield with a win for the first time since September 2012.

There were some nervy moments, with Liverpool on top and piling on the pressure for large periods, but Arsenal just about held firm.

Standard Sport’s Matt Verri was at Anfield to rate the Arsenal players...

One sensational pass through to Martin Odegaard broke the Liverpool press. Did just about enough to put Alexander Isak off and stop him finishing from a corner. For all the pressure Liverpool put on Arsenal, he did not have a save to make.

Incredibly lucky to not concede a penalty for a very obvious tug of Isak’s shirt. So adventurous in attack, often the most advanced player. Tireless shift and rescued his side with a last-ditch block on Ronald Araujo from close range.

Looked rattled at times early on but he stepped up massively in an incredible second-half display. A pivotal block to deny Florian Wirtz but plenty in the highlights reel beyond that. Won all seven ground duels. Massive performance when Arsenal needed it most.

Angered Liverpool fans with how often he went down. Fairly quiet afternoon by his standards, with Konsa more in the thick of it, but more than played his part in dragging Arsenal to an ugly, hard-fought win.

Sometimes a bit too frantic on the ball when Arsenal needed calm but he showed he can be a complete left-back with this outstanding defensive display. Gave Cody Gakpo and then Rio Ngumoha nothing. Shifted to wing-back for closing minutes.

Yet another monster effort in midfield. Great overlapping run and perfect cross created Havertz’s goal. Intercepted brilliantly in his own box when Bradley Barcola looked to be in. Mopped up and shielded the defence. A machine.

His kind of occasion. Roared at the away fans after one huge challenge to halt Barcola. Snapped into the challenges and relished the red-hot atmosphere, but began to tire and looked vulnerable when Liverpool ran in midfield. Replaced after an hour.

Led the Arsenal press exceptionally in a really bright start and it created the opener as he won it back. But Arsenal needed more on the ball and there was not enough control to ease the pressure, with flicks not coming off.

Surprise inclusion in the starting lineup but delivered for Mikel Arteta. Impressive how sharp and bright he was, and clipped one superb cross to the back post that should have been converted. Too unselfish at points but also denied by a sensational Alisson save.

Perfect response to his wasteful run when he tapped in to open the scoring. So often shows on the biggest stage and did so again. Overall performance was not his best and he was far too keen to go to ground, but a winner at Anfield is a huge moment.

#1858. Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Emery said: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

Their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

Villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Villa defended resolutely as time began to tick away with Suzuki providing authority in goal. The first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League also produced a number of routine saves in a nervy finish.

This was a promising night for a new Villa era.

Full-time scenes in Bruges as Aston Villa get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nYwtiQ6Xs7

Villa are defending with six at the back as midfield and defence merge into one. There are seconds remaining as Suzuki punts the ball up field and there is the final whistle! Villa make a winning start to the 2026-27 Champions League.

Another cross from the right is met, this time, by Tresoldi, but his header has no bite and Suzuki gathers.

Torres heads another Siquet cross behind for a corner. Brugge load the box but none of their players are able to get a meaningful touch on the ball before Diakhon slips just as he looks to get a shot away from the left of the box.

Slightly less mature play from Gomes, though. He bundles Vermant over and earns a needless yellow card.

Really mature play by Hemmings. Looking to break away, he simply puts his body between man and ball, inviting the challenge and winning a foul.

Villa are working hard in their compact mid-block and Brugge are struggling to find a way through.

Leko sends on Vermant and Diakhon for Potts and Virgili.

Barkley is one lucky boy. Attempting to play out under pressure, the midfielder gives the ball straight to Virgili, who cannot sort out his feet before offloading to Tresoldi far too late. A big let-off for Villa.

Gomes goes close after driving through Brugge’s midfield. He really should, though, have played in a free McGinn at the back post. Moments later Bogarde fires another shot goalwards but Sommer gets to it.

Villa have wrestled control away from their opponents. McGinn’s teasing cross evades everyone and Alysson’s cross takes a deflection which goes behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Lee hauls down Hemmings which gives Villa the opportunity to slow the game down. McGinn flights a delivery in from the left but Brugge clear their lines.

The ball comes out to Alysson who jinks in from the right, tiptoeing through a crowd, desperate to get a shot away on his left foot, but Seys does well to track his man and smother the effort.

Vanakan and Velesen and replaced by Tsawa and Lemarechal.

Yet another dangerous Siquet cross rains in from the right and here it is taken off Tresoldi’s toes by the tip of Lindelof’s boot. The defender did brilliantly to clear his lines at full stretch.

Hemmings burst towards the by-line and his cross trickles across the face of goal. Alysson is waiting at the far post but Seys does well to shield the ball and win a free-kick.

Villa’s best chance at putting this game to bed will come on the counter. And here McGinn plays in Jackson whose one-vs-one effort is stopped by Sommer.

Virgili from the left, Siquet from the right. Threats are coming from both wings and Villa need to get their foot on the ball if they are to take the sting out of Brugge’s attack.

Instead they allow Vetlesen a yard of space and his long-range sighter stings the hands of Suzuki who turns behind for a corner.

Emery switches out Buendia, Kamara and Wan-Bissaka for Alysson, Barkley and Bogarde before the corner is taken, and Suzuki stops the eventual delivery on the line after the ball spun off the post!

Another Virgili cross threatens to carve Villa open but they just about clear their lines. Then it is Siquet who delivers, this time from the right, but his cross just evades Tresoldi and Mechele at the far post. The home fans are invested in this, they believe their side can grab an equaliser...

Villa have got their tails between their legs here. From a position of strength, they have allowed the momentum to swing in the hosts’ favour and it has been largely self-inflicted.

Maatsen has a chance to break free but cannot build a head of steam before he is stymied.

Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3 (Tresoldi pen) Suzuki dives to his right early and Tresoldi slides the ball into the opposite side of the net. Just the one goal in it now!

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Brugge have averted their attention to their right hand side, Siquet and Forbs attacking in tandem. A dangerous cross from Forbs is met by Tresoldi but he cannot get the requisite contact on it. Seys collects the ball on the far side and fires a delivery into Wan-Bissaka and out for a corner. Replays show that it comes off the defenders hand ...and referee Scharer is sent to the screen. He wastes no time at the monitor and awards a spot kick!

Villa do appear pretty comfortable here, despite some frequent pressure from Club Brugge.

Pau Torres has been outstanding so far at the back for Unai Emery’s team.

This is also a night where Emery’s ‘new’ Villa are coming of age, with Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and Joao Gomes also impressive.

Virgili then darts in field from his starting perch on the left. Tresoldi backheels the ball back into his path but Virgili’s effort is snuffed out.

McGinn, sensing Virgili’s growing influence on the half, takes matters into his own hands and leaves one on the Spanish winger, Siquet’s free-kick from deep is aimed at Tresoldi but Suzuki is wise to it and sweeps up.

Brugge are just reminding Villa that they are still there. Virgili is at the heart of things again, combining with Vetlesen who works the ball out to Forbs whose cross is well held by Suzuki.

Villa then spring forward, Hemmings breaching the Brugge box, but Buendia’s eventual effort does not make it through a thicket of legs.

Brugge are building with a three-man backline, sending Siquet forward high and wide. They’ve had much of the ball in the opening stages of this half, which is probably part of Villa’s plan. Emery’s side have settled into an out-of-possession 4-4-2.

Vanakan is booked for simulation after going hitting the deck off a challenge from Gomes. There is a knowing smile on the Belgian midfielder’s face which suggests the referee’s convictions were correct.

We are back under way... Siquet replaces Sabbe at the interval.

Nicolas Jackson is off the mark for Aston Villa. He beat Yann Sommer to the ball, held off a defender and was left with the simplest of finishes to round off a fine first half for Villa. pic.twitter.com/gWx6kUTlOX

Unai Emery has the new kids on the block but this Aston Villa team are hangin’ tough.

This has been a pretty chaotic first-half on the return of the Champions League but Emery will be satisfied with what he has seen so far. It’s very much a case of step by step for his reshaped team, but they should see this game out now.

It’s been a shocking night for Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper Yann Sommer. He’s just had a serious rush of blood to the head and was punished by Nicolas Jackson, who had an easy task to score Villa’s third goal. Sommer has probably ended his team’s hopes of a result here.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 3 (Jackson) A shocker from Brugge, but in particular Sommer. Jackson races on to a nothing punt over the top by Torres, and the situation appears under control with two defenders in the striker’s orbit, but Sommer comes steaming out and Jackson nudges the ball past him before sliding it home into a vacant net.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

A sloppy Torres pass out from the back goes straight to Vetlesen who picks out Forbs first time. The winger unleashes an effort from range but Suzuki makes a smart stop.

There is a shout for a Villa handball as Virgili prods a cross on to Kamara’s body, but his arms are clearly by his side.

Villa are presented with a great opportunity to break but the pass in behind for Jackson to gallop on to does not have enough juice and the move breaks down. Jackson does have a sight at goal moments later, but he’s only able to poke the ball wide off a free-kick from the right.

A really sloppy piece bit of play from Vanakan who cedes possession to Jackson and he’s straight into Brugge’s backline. He releases the ball to McGinn but the midfielder’s looping cross is cleared. Brugge need to take better care with the detail on their passes.

Jackson escapes the clutches of his marker on the half-way line with a deft spin and he feeds McGinn whose shot is blocked. The ball is worked to Hemmings after Torres is afforded space once more and a block takes it behind for a corner. Villa go short but the routine comes to nothing.

Maatsen flashes a dangerous delivery across the face of goal but the ball bisects Jackson and Buendia precisely and Brugge are able to clear their lines.

Brugge have certainly not given up the ghost, still looking to work the ball out to Forbs and Virgili on the flanks. Sabbe overlaps down the right but his ball to Vetlesen is cut out and Villa attempt to spring a counter which is snuffed out by Mechele.

Villa midfielder Joao Gomes is having a productive evening as he aims to recover from that nightmare debut.

He was sent off after 40 minutes of his first Villa appearance in the excruciating 4-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion.

Unai Emery is expecting big things from the Brazilian midfielder, who departed relegated Wolves for £38m in July.

Wan-Bissaka drives down the right as Villa look for a third, but his cross is overhit and goes off on the far side. The right intent, though.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 2 (Buendia) Jackson holds up the ball expertly before slipping in Gomes. The midfielder bursts into the box, outwitting Vetlesen before cutting the ball back to an onrushing Buendia who clips the ball past Sommer with aplomb. A crazy couple of minutes!

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 1 (Vetlesen) Brugge are getting a lot of joy down the flanks. This time it is Vetlesen who finds space down the right and he spears a cross into the box. The ball is worked out to the left where the dangerous Virgili sends the ball back into the area and there Vetlesen is to sweep home. The stadium erupts as the Belgian champions restore parity.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

The Jan Breydelstadion had been very noisy but that goal has completely changed the atmosphere.

It is now nervy in the stadium and the Brugge fans are already starting to boo some of their players.

Villa’s first goal of the season and no surprise it comes from their talisman John McGinn.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

Close! Hemmings races on to a cutback but his effort trickles just wide of the post.

Goalkeeper Sommer is penalised for handling the ball outside of his box. He had gathered a corner and had stormed forward to set off an attack. He changes his mind mid-throw and attempts to re-catch the ball but ends up wandering outside of his allotted space. The resulting free-kick crashes straight into the wall.

Sommer with an accidental handball outside his area! 😳📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fBbqPEYyUJ

Club Brugge 0 Aston Villa 1 (McGinn) Brugge will be really disappointed with that. Torres is afforded the freedom of Flanders as he strides up from his own half to the edge of the hosts’ box. He offloads the ball to McGinn on the right of the area and the Scotsman steadies himself before curling the ball into the far post, beyond Sommer.

It is that duo again, Virgili and Seys. They have responded to Wan-Bissaka’s advanced position and are trying to pin him back. Virgili cuts in on to his right foot and forces a save from Suzuki to get the home fans going.

Aston Villa are still establishing their identity with a new team but it has already become clear how much they will rely on goalkeeper Zion Suzuki,

The £30m signing from Parma possesses a wide passing range and much of Villa’s build-up play starts with the Japan international.

He is Villa’s very own version of Manchester City’s former pass master Ederson.

Much has been made of Suzuki’s distribution and he has already teased a couple of lovely flighted balls up-field. Villa’s defenders are more than happy to lure Brugge’s first line of pressure forward but have not yet been able to find an incisive line-breaking pass.

Seyes and Virgili combine down the left in Brugge’s best attack so far, but Torres is able to head behind for a corner, which is not up to much.

Wan-Bissaka has taken up a very aggressive position down Villa’s right and he earns a free-kick in a promising position. McGinn spins in a delivery which is only partially cleared but Maatsen’s effort from the edge of the box is smothered.

Villa get their foot on the ball from the get-go, circulating the ball around the back, before Suzuki launches a long ball up to Wan-Bissaka. The ball is worked to McGinn who feeds Buendia on the edge of the box but his effort flies just wide.

There is a minute’s silence for those affected by the floods in Nepal which is impeccably observed.

The players then retreat to their halves and Jackson gets us going!

Brugge and Villa emerge from the tunnel to the Champions League anthem... Here is this season’s introductory VT to whet the appetite.

The Champions League is back. #UCL pic.twitter.com/bsFGV69KMP

"This is a good test and challenge for us today." 💪Aston Villa boss Unai Emery looks ahead to their Champions League clash with Club Brugge.🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h4NF1jmiW6

As the rain lashes down in Bruges, you get the sense that Villa will have to dig deep to get a result and breathe life into their season. Both teams thrive on attacking transitions and the surface-level moisture will encourage breakaway moves.

Sep 8: Club Brugge vs Aston VillaOct 14: Aston Villa vs Fenerbahçe Oct 21: Aston Villa vs Viking Nov 3: Barcelona vs Aston VillaNov 24: Galatasaray vs Aston Villa Dec 8: Aston Villa vs Paris St-Germain Jan 19: Aston Villa vs Borussia DortmundJan 27: Slavia Praha vs Aston Villa

Quite the evening, last time out at the Jan Breydel Stadium 💫 pic.twitter.com/NogGLLSMFU

Opta’s supercomputer has worked its magic again this season and placed Villa as the 10th favourites to lift the Champions League trophy. Back-to-back winners Paris St-Germain are only fifth. Here are the leading contenders before a ball has been kicked.

Agree? Leave your thoughts in the comments section beneath this live blog...

Aston Villa 2.0 is clearly a work in progress after so many high-profile exits and 10 new signings.

Unai Emery has warned that it will take time for his new team to click, but this is an opportunity to spark the season into life.

Behind the scenes, Villa are feeling very comfortable about so much upheaval and it is the presence of Emery in the technical area which provides them with so much optimism.

For a deeper dive into why patience will be needed, read more here.

Brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

Here are a couple of examples of Brugge’s vulnerability down their right:

Don-Angelo Konadu, Lommel’s centre-forward, drifts out to the left and takes on Lee Han-beom whose centre-back partner Brandon Mechele has committed too far forward. As such, the space between Lee and covering left-back Joaquin Seys is too big and Freddie Potts attempts to recover from midfield. Konadu earns himself a yard with a feint inside and his shot is well-saved by Yann Sommer.

In Brugge’s 2-1 defeat by Gent a week earlier, Leonardo Lopes punches in a pass into the left half-space for Monodu Sonko to latch on to and from there the inside forward draws a save from Sommer. Josué Vergara’s follow-up strikes the crossbar.

The Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today announced as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

Christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

While Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

He was signed from West Ham last month for a significant fee and lifted the Europa Conference League trophy when David Moyes was in charge.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

Club Brugge Sommer; Sabbe, Lee, Mechele, Seys; Potts, Vanaken; Forbs, Vetlesen, Virgili; Tresoldi

Substitutes Audoor, Coulibaly, Diakhon, Jackers, Lemarechal, Mike, Siquet, Spileers, Tsawa, Vanden Driessche, Vasovic, Vermant

Aston Villa Suzuki; Wan-Bissaka, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Buendia, Hemmings; Jackson

Substitutes Abraham, Barkley, Bizot, Bogarde, Garnacho, Mbaye, Mings, Ruggeri, Wright, Alysson

One player who will have many memories of this stadium is Villa centre-back Tyrone Mings.

Who can forget that bewildering moment in November 2024 when Mings picked up the ball inside the penalty area?

Club Brugge are awarded a penalty after Tyrone Mings picks the ball up inside his own area 😳📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/wpAqjMW8pn

Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

Mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle issue so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He said: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

“We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [big] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

“We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a new test.”

The experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Our ground crew for tonight. 👥📃 pic.twitter.com/UB7FUi9ZDH

Emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a new-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of big-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s new-look crew.

Morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his new recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

#1857. Tottenham youngster set for international call-up after impressing Roberto De Zerbi

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham midfielder Tyrese Hall is set to be called up by Jamaica ahead of their two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie against Mexico this month.

The 21-year-old, who has been training regularly with Roberto De Zerbi’s first team at Spurs this season, has two senior international caps for Jamaica and made his debut in March this year.

The Reggae Boyz will first host Mexico in Kingston on Sunday, November 15 before travelling to play the second leg three days later.

Hall has been in and around Spurs’ first team setup this season but has yet to make his senior debut for the club, and Standard Sport understands there is likely to be loan and permanent interest in the former England youth international when the January transfer window opens.

Hall was expected to leave Tottenham on loan in the summer, but a deal failed to materialise before the deadline, and he joined back up with Wayne Burnett’s Under-21s team.

His impressive performances for the U21s caught the attention of De Zerbi, and he travelled with the first team for their warm-weather training camp in Marbella last month.

Jamaica’s interim manager Rudolph Speid picked Hall for the March internationals as part of a new data-driven approach to squad selection.

Hall became the first Spurs player ever to represent Jamaica when he made his senior international debut by coming off the bench in a World Cup play-off match against DR Congo.

He was called up again in May and made his full debut, playing 90 minutes as Jamaica beat India 2-0 in the Unity Cup, which was held at The Valley, home of Charlton.

#1855. Bayern to be cautious with Olise ahead of trip to Atletico

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Bayern Munich director Max Eberl insisted the club will not rush Michael Olise back from injury to avoid a potential long-term issue.

Olise was replaced late on during Bayern's Klassiker draw with Borussia Dortmund on Saturday with a knee injury.

The winger trained with strapping around his knee on Monday, and has travelled with the squad ahead of their Champions League clash with Atletico Madrid, though his participation is in question.

Olise has scored 12 goals and provided six assists in 13 appearances for Bayern this season, while only Lamine Yamal (23) and Raphinha (20) have directly contributed to more goals across the top five European leagues.

Manuel Neuer is also an injury doubt for Tuesday's clash, and Eberl offered an update on both the goalkeeper and Olise.

"As for Michael Olise, we'll take another look at him on Tuesday; we're taking it day by day," Eberl said.

"It's good that he's travelling with us, because he's an outstanding player who's always a great asset. However, we’ll avoid the risk of it turning into a long-term injury.

"Manuel Neuer has been out for quite some time but has been training, so we'll see how it goes."

All set for masterpiece in Madrid  https://t.co/HV4O8C3JaX

— FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) November 2, 2026

Bayern have drawn their last two games in this competition (3-3 v Viking, 2-2 v Arsenal), and have not drawn three in a row in the Champions League for almost 20 years, last doing so between October-December 2006 (three).

Despite winning just two of their eight meetings against Bayern in European competition, Atleti are unbeaten against them at home (W2 D1).

Harry Kane, who has scored in each of his last 10 appearances for Bayern in the Champions League, anticipates a tough challenge in the Spanish capital.

"They're a very strong side; they’re very good defensively," Kane said of Atleti.

"So, you might think only of their defence – but they're also good going forward. They enjoy playing football, especially in attack. And they've got some very dangerous players, [so] we won’t be underestimating them.

"We're expecting it to be a very physical game. That's one of their strengths. But we need to be careful at the back; we hope we can improve a few things."

#1854. High school soccer referee left with a collapsed lung and broken ribs after vicious attack by player

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 20:42 EDT, 28 October 2026 | Updated: 20:45 EDT, 28 October 2026

An Ohio high school soccer referee was left seriously injured after being inexplicably tackled by a player during a playoff game this week.

The barely-believable incident occurred during a district matchup between New Philadelphia and Steubenville on Tuesday night.

New Philadelphia's 2-1 victory was overshadowed by the ugly scenes when the official was bodychecked to the ground by one of the players.

The offending player, who appeared to be a member of Steubenville's team, was seemingly left frustrated after one of his teammates was shown a red card.

In viral footage shared by Bob Greenburg on X, the unassuming referee could be seen walking away after booking the teammate when the player inexplicably ran into the back of him.

The unidentified player was captured charging at the running official before driving head-first into the referee's midriff and leaving him sprawled on the turf.

A high school soccer referee was left injured after being tackled to the ground by a player

The official was taken to hospital where he is being treated for broken ribs and a collapsed lung, according to TMZ.

The Ohio High School Athletic Association is yet to announce a formal punishment to the player over the shocking incident but it vowed that the consequences will be significant - and most definitely worse than a red card.

'The OHSAA is waiting for a response from the school to announce the discipline that the school will take against the student-athlete, which will determine if the OHSAA will issue additional penalties,' a spokesperson for the organization told The Daily Mail.

'The school has indicated that punishment will be significant, which the OHSAA agrees with. Physical violence against an official is among the most serious offenses that a coach, player or fan can commit and the OHSAA will pursue this to the fullest extent possible.'

'The Steubenville City Schools is aware of the incident involving a student and a game official following a recent athletic contest,' a spokesperson for the Steubenville Board of Education told The Daily Mail in a statement.

'The District worked collaboratively with the Ohio High School Athletic Association (OHSAA) to review the matter and ensure it was addressed appropriately.

The offending player was seen charging at the official before driving head-first into him

'The District remains committed to maintaining high standards of sportsmanship, respect, and safety at all athletic events.'

New Philadelphia traveled to Steubenville for the Division III level clash on Tuesday with the two schools separated by just 60 miles.

Thanks to their win, New Philadelphia will now face Dover in the District Final on Thursday evening with a place in the Regional Semifinals on the line.

Steubenville and their reckless player, meanwhile, were eliminated from the playoffs by Tuesday night's result.

#1853. Manchester United handed huge boost in bid for crucial Roma win after new update

Manchester United’s hopes of finally ending their long winless run under Michael Carrick appear to have been boosted by Roma’s ongoing injury problems.

The Serie A giants head to Old Trafford for Tuesday night’s high-profile Champions League tie missing a number of key stars.

Head coach Gian Piero Gasperini admitted at Monday’s pre-match press conference that he had brought only 17 outfield players with him to Manchester as Roma continue to struggle with a hectic fixture schedule.

Paulo Dybala, Mile Svilar, Manu Kone and Lorenzo Pellegrini are among the Giallorossi contingent to have been absent of late, though it has not affected results as they arrive in England having won four of their last five matches across all competitions - including Saturday’s 5-2 thrashing of struggling Udinese in Serie A, which took them up to third.

That is in stark contrast to Manchester United, whose current nine-game winless run is their worst sequence since 1988/89 as the club are once again plunged into crisis with another manager pushed to the brink.

The under-fire Carrick will remain in charge for the visit of Roma despite a third successive defeat at the hands of Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, with Aston Villa also visiting Old Trafford before the next international break begins.

However, it has been reported that his position will be reviewed again after that, making the next two matches absolutely critical.

“Obviously Manchester United is struggling somewhat in terms of results in the Premier League at the moment,” Gasperini said on Monday evening.

“But we can’t get distracted and too hung up on that situation because we know that Manchester United is a strong team, we know that they have top players in their squad. We know what the atmosphere is going to be like here as well.

“They make things very difficult for the opposition here at Old Trafford, so we’ll be playing tomorrow’s game as if we’re playing against Manchester United at the top of its form.

#1852. Jamie Carragher makes bold new Arsenal claim after Liverpool masterclass

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal showed against Liverpool that they are the the best defensive team in all of world football, according to Jamie Carragher.

The Gunners pulled off what Gary Neville hailed as a “masterclass” on Sunday to win a Premier League game at Anfield for the first time since September 2012 and move three points clear at the summit.

Kai Havertz slotted in the only goal of a heavyweight clash on Merseyside in the 16th minute after superb work from midfield duo Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard, but the three points owed much to Arsenal’s efforts at the other end of the pitch.

Though they rode their luck at times with Liverpool denied what should have been a clear penalty for Jurrien Timber’s shirt pull on Alexander Isak in the first half, Mikel Arteta’s side delivered a sublime defensive display.

Despite the Reds dominating most of the match after falling behind and registering a total of 33 crosses and 17 shots, they failed to produce a single effort on target.

It was the first time that has happened to them in a league game at Anfield since records began in 2003 - a run of 442 consecutive home top-flight matches.

“This Arsenal team are the best defensive team not just in the Premier League, but I think in world football right now,” Liverpool legend Carragher said in his role as a pundit on Monday Night Football for Sky Sports.

Much of the praise for Arsenal’s winning goal against Liverpool has gone to Rice for his driving run and perfect delivery for Havertz to sweep home from close range at the back post, but Carragher gave special plaudits to Odegaard for leading a suffocating press that saw the hosts quickly cough up possession in their own half following a short goal kick - which has been a notable problem area in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if the plan was for [Alexis] Mac Allister to stay high and allow [Jeremy] Jacquet to step in, but it is brilliant from Odegaard, you have to say that,” Carragher said.

“Great press from [Christos] Tzolis and Odegaard is really brave. He’s almost quicker to the ball than Mac Allister is but again, that’s something only the Liverpool team know. It’s a fantastic ball from Declan Rice.

“It’s poor from Liverpool, but brilliant from Arsenal. The plan would always have been that when the ball goes into Mac Allister, Odegaard it’s your job to get after him.

“The way we saw Fulham do it, the way we saw Brighton do it. It was just that they won the ball in a different part of the pitch.”

#1851. Prediction: Feyenoord vs Inter Milan

Feyenoord and Inter Milan enter Tuesday’s Champions League clash knowing that three points could significantly boost their chances of reaching the knockout stage.

Both former European champions have collected just three points from their opening three league-phase matches and can afford few more slip-ups as the competition approaches its halfway point.

Feyenoord’s Champions League campaign has been a mixed one so far.

The Dutch champions began with a heavy 5-1 defeat to Barcelona before bouncing back with an entertaining 3-2 victory over Como. However, they were unable to build on that success, suffering a narrow 1-0 loss at Real Betis in their most recent European fixture.

Those results leave Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s side on three points and under increasing pressure to make their home advantage count.

Recent domestic performances have provided more encouragement. Feyenoord remain among the Eredivisie frontrunners and continue to be exceptionally difficult to beat at De Kuip, where the atmosphere remains one of the most intimidating in European football.

The hosts also possess several dangerous attacking players. Anis Hadj Moussa has emerged as a key threat, while captain Luciano Valente and striker Nacho Ferri continue to provide goals and creativity.

Injury concerns remain relatively manageable, although Bart Nieuwkoop, Jordan Bos and Thomas Beelen are still unavailable. Jeremiah St. Juste faces a late fitness test.

Inter arrive in Rotterdam under pressure after another turbulent week.

Cristian Chivu’s side suffered a painful 3-1 defeat against AC Milan in the Derby della Madonnina, extending a disappointing run in one of Italian football’s biggest fixtures. That result also highlighted some of the defensive issues that have plagued Inter in recent European competitions.

The Nerazzurri’s Champions League campaign has been similarly inconsistent. After defeats to Real Madrid and Club Brugge, they finally collected their first points with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Shakhtar Donetsk despite finishing the match with 10 men.

Inter’s recent European record is surprisingly poor for a club that reached the Champions League final in both 2023 and 2025. They have now lost seven of their last nine matches in the competition and remain some way below the standards expected of them.

Captain Lautaro Martinez is unavailable, while Luis Henrique, Benjamin Pavard, John Stones and Curtis Jones are also sidelined. Alessandro Bastoni will miss the game through suspension.

Marcus Thuram is expected to lead the attack, potentially alongside either Pio Esposito or Ange Bonny if they recover fully from recent illness.

This feels like a pivotal fixture for both sides. Feyenoord’s home form and the intense atmosphere at De Kuip make them difficult opponents, particularly for an Inter side arriving with injuries, suspensions and declining confidence.

However, the Italian club still possess considerable quality, especially in attacking areas, and should create plenty of opportunities against a Feyenoord defence that has rarely looked completely secure in Europe.

Expect an open and entertaining contest between two sides who know a draw does little for either. Feyenoord’s home advantage may be enough to avoid defeat, but Inter’s attacking talent should ensure they leave Rotterdam with something.

Prediction: Borussia Dortmund vs Real Betis

#1850. Chelsea injury update: Joao Pedro, Jordan Henderson, Emi Martinez latest news and return dates

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea have several key injury issues persisting after their win over Manchester United as attentions now turn towards a trip to Sunderland.

The Blues claimed a much-needed 2-0 victory against Michael Carrick’s crisis-stricken side at Stamford Bridge in Saturday’s high-profile lunchtime Premier League kick-off.

Morgan Rogers scored a brilliant solo goal to finally break the deadlock early in the second half following another below-par first 45 minutes from Chelsea, with Cole Palmer then marking his return from a one-match suspension by narrowly dispatching a penalty after Lisandro Martinez was sent off for a foul on Wesley Fofana.

Estevao saw two goals disallowed for offside after being handed a rare start by Xabi Alonso, whose team bounced back after a Carabao Cup last-16 exit on penalties at Liverpool that quickly followed only a second home league defeat by rivals Tottenham in 36 years.

Alonso’s side will fancy their chances of making it back-to-back victories against a Sunderland outfit who sit rock bottom of the table after being brushed aside by newly-promoted Coventry last time out. Here is all the latest Chelsea injury news and return dates.

Joao Pedro was a surprise absentee from the Chelsea squad for their rare home loss to Tottenham, with Alonso later confirming that he had picked up a thigh injury in training on the eve of the game.

No definitive timeframe has yet been set for the return of the star striker, top scorer and reigning Player of the Season, who also saw a specialist last month to speed up his recovery from a knee problem.

Chelsea will be understandably cautious with such an important player, who seems unlikely to play again before the November international break.

“He has an injury on his thigh and he's going be out for a few weeks," Alonso said on Joao Pedro before the defeat by Liverpool. "Let's see how many. We don't want to predict on that. But not ready for the next games.

“He's a key player. We will miss him, but we have to be ready to deal with the injury, and be competitive and try and win with the players we have available. This is the situation.”

Talking of surprise absentees, Jordan Henderson was unexpectedly absent from the Chelsea squad to face Manchester United, despite having played 90 minutes against former club Liverpool in midweek and become a mainstay of Alonso’s midfield engine room of late alongside Moises Caicedo.

However, the manager allayed any concerns over an injury to his veteran summer signing, whom he said was ill and suffering with a fever on Saturday.

“He's ill," Alonso said of Henderson to TNT Sports. “There's no injury, but he was not feeling well yesterday and today had a fever in the morning, so he was not feeling good enough to come with the team.”

Emi Martinez needed lengthy treatment on the pitch and was stretchered off following a sickening accidental clash of heads with England defender Jarrad Branthwaite during Chelsea’s 2-0 win at Everton last month.

The Argentine goalkeeper was quickly taken to hospital and underwent successful surgery to repair what was confirmed to be a broken jaw, leaving him staring at a potential lengthy layoff.

However, Martinez’s progress since then has been swift and he’s pushing to return ahead of schedule, with Alonso admitting that there’s a chance he could be back before the international break - likely wearing a face mask.

No2 Mike Penders has deputised for Chelsea in Martinez’s absence, scoring an unfortunate own goal on his first Premier League start against Tottenham but making an incredible stoppage-time save to deny Bryan Mbeumo in the win over Manchester United.

“Yes, there is a chance,” Alonso said of Martinez possibly playing before the next international window. “We need to still wait for next week, but let’s see how things go. But there is a chance.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 8, vs Sunderland (A)

Chelsea’s influential captain Reece James suffered a knee injury in training at Cobham on his return from another hamstring issue.

After consulting with a specialist, he underwent successful surgery last month that was described as “minor” and Alonso has been reluctant to put a date on his potential return.

However, Standard Sport understands that it is likely to be around three months before James is back in action.

Maxence Lacroix limped off late in the first half at Liverpool with a worrying-looking hamstring injury.

Alonso said that Chelsea would need to assess the problem before estimating a recovery time, later admitting that he would be out until after the November international break.

“Max picked up an injury and we expect that he will not be ready before the international break. So he will be a few weeks out,” Alonso said before the win over Manchester United.

Reports have since suggested that Chelsea fear Lacroix, like James, may not play again until the New Year.

Jorrel Hato had been filling in at left wing-back during the absence of Pep Chavarria, who returned off the bench against Manchester United.

However, he was a surprise absentee from the squad that travelled to Liverpool and was not available against United either after Alonso revealed that the Dutchman was battling a back injury.

“How long, we don't know, but he’s not available for tomorrow,” Alonso said. “He has a back problem and he's not feeling okay for tomorrow.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 8, vs Sunderland (A)

Jamie Gittens has yet to make a single Premier League appearance for Chelsea so far this season, with his only two outings to date coming against Luton and Leeds in the Carabao Cup.

The winger has been so unlucky with injuries since arriving in west London from Borussia Dortmund last summer, a trend which continued as he suffered an ankle problem while on international duty with England’s Under-21s last month and needed crutches.

Alonso’s last update confirmed that Gittens was still facing “weeks” on the sidelines, putting him on track to return at some point in November or perhaps even early December.

Potential return date: November or December

Young defender Aaron Anselmino has become something of a forgotten man among Chelsea fans after a bit-part role during pre-season that followed an injury-ruined loan spell at BlueCo sister club Strasbourg during the second half of last term.

He had been enjoying a productive stint in Germany with Borussia Dortmund before that.

“He is not available yet,” Alonso said of Anselmino last week. “He has had a few things, a few injuries, and it will take a few weeks until he is fully fit. We need to be cautious with him as he's had a few of them, so he is still not there.”

Potential return date: November or December

#1849. Castillejo predicts Musah and Ramos to score in Milan-Inter: “A 2-1 win”

Samu Castillejo, the former Milan player, has provided his prediction for tonight’s Derby della Madonnina against Inter.

Castillejo recently announced his retirement from professional football and it was news that certainly reached the Milan world. Spending four years at the club, including winning the Scudetto in 2021-22, he’s a player that most fans remember fondly.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He featured in four derbies against Inter and also faced the Nerazzurri during his spell at Sassuolo, so he knows what it’s like to face them. Speaking to Sky Italia, as transcribed by MilanPress, he shared his thoughts on tonight’s edition of the Derby della Madonnina.

“The derby is always a special match. You don’t care about the standings or the points, you only think about the match and you can’t wait to play. It’s a match you start to feel from the first few days of the week.

“We have seen many derbies where Milan were in better form and then didn’t win, and vice versa. It’s never easy to play; the atmosphere matters a lot.”

“Obviously, I hope Milan win. I’m predicting a 2-1 win with a goal from Goncalo Ramos. He hasn’t started well, but he’s a very strong striker. Then I’d say my friend Musah, whom I played with at Valencia,” he concluded.

It’s perhaps a little bit of a rogue prediction when you consider that Goncalo Ramos hasn’t scored in the league since the end of August. Yunus Musah is also yet to get off the mark this season, so it would be quite something if they were to decide the derby tonight.
