#1848. Arsenal 'want two major new signings' as top Mikel Arteta targets revealed

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal have Eli Junior Kroupi and Kenan Yildiz firmly on their transfer radar ahead of the January window, new reports claim.

Bournemouth forward Kroupi was understood to have been a prominent target for the Gunners during the summer, only to suffer a foot fracture during pre-season that required surgery.

The France Under-21 international was sidelined for three months, halting his significant momentum after a fantastic debut season in English football following a move from Lorient in which he netted 13 goals in 35 appearances across all competitions.

However, Kroupi has played in Bournemouth’s last three matches as a substitute after returning to fitness and will be bidding to make a first start under Marco Rose as the Cherries travel to Sparta Prague in the Europa League and Ipswich in the Premier League prior to the November international break.

Kroupi’s return to action has led to renewed transfer talk, with The Mirror reporting that Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta is bidding to strengthen his attacking options in January amid interest in the 20-year-old.

The Gunners are also said to be keen on Yildiz, the Juventus winger who has been frequently linked with a switch to north London over recent windows and was subject to more speculation during the latter stages of the summer.

However, as with Kroupi, who is also said to be interesting a range of other clubs including Manchester United, Tottenham, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain, those rumours were quickly dashed by a foot fracture sustained in late August that required surgery. The Turkey star has not featured since, having made just one Serie A appearance so far this term.

Signing either Kroupi or Yildiz in January will potentially prove difficult for Arsenal, who welcomed the likes of Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis, Ezri Konsa, Piero Hincapie and Illan Meslier during a busy summer window but were unsuccessful in their pursuit of other high-profile targets such as Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez.

It has been widely reported on multiple occasions that Bournemouth will not entertain the possibility of selling Kroupi mid-season, especially with England midfielder Alex Scott potentially leaving in January amid a transfer U-turn and likely bidding war between Chelsea and Liverpool.

Juventus head coach Luciano Spalletti emphatically ruled out the prospect of a departure from Turin for Yildiz in the summer, insisting it did not matter if interested clubs were willing to offer €100million.

#1847. Jordan Henderson smirks as he trolls Anfield boo-boys on return with Chelsea - and argues with ex-Liverpool team-mate Virgil van Dijk

Published: 19:47 EDT, 28 October 2026 | Updated: 20:51 EDT, 28 October 2026

Jordan Henderson laughed off his haters on his return to Anfield on Wednesday night.

Liverpool legend Henderson, 36, played the full 90 minutes of the Carabao Cup last-16 tie as Chelsea lost 6-5 on penalties, although the veteran did score his spot kick.

It capped what must have been a strange night for the midfielder as he went back to the club where he made 492 appearances and won eight trophies over a 12-year period. Henderson left to join Saudi Arabian side Al-Ettifaq in the summer of 2023.

Despite his long service, Henderson received a vociferous reception as a Chelsea player, with the home faithful booing him every time he touched the ball.

And, after the Blues were awarded a penalty in the first half when Ryan Gravenberch fouled Moises Caicedo, that atmosphere escalated further.

Henderson picked up the ball and walked towards the penalty spot as if he was going to take the spot kick.

Hendo smirking at Liverpool fans in a Chelsea shirt. Never thought we'd see the daypic.twitter.com/Fac2gSbe5x

Jordan Henderson was seen smirking after receiving a hostile reception from Liverpool fans

The former Liverpool captain also argued with his former team-mate Virgil van Dijk at one point

As he did so, Henderson was loudly jeered and he allowed himself a wry smile and laugh as he looked back towards the crowd.

Henderson ultimately handed the ball over to Morgan Rogers, who made no mistake from the spot.

The hostile reception may have been in part motivated by the midfielder's desire to contest several decisions with Liverpool's players and referee Darren England, along with the fact he is now representing Chelsea.

At one point early in the first half, both Henderson and his former team-mate Virgil van Dijk fought their case in one discussion with England.

As they walked away, the pair shouted at each other from afar in what must have been a strange sight for Liverpool supporters to witness.

Henderson did later appear to applaud the crowd after the game when he was also seen laughing and joking with van Dijk.

Meanwhile, at the end of last season, Henderson, who has similarly played for Ajax and Brentford in recent years, returned to Anfield for the first time with the Bees.

On that occasion, he received a warm reception and then a standing ovation when he was substituted in the second half.

Speaking after that game, he wrote on social media: 'I'd like to thank the Liverpool fans for the reception they gave me yesterday.

'It meant a lot to me going back to Anfield and being able to say thank you for everything you gave me in my 12 years at the club. It's a feeling that I'll never forget.

'To be able to be there to see my two brothers, Mo [Salah] and Robbo [Andy Robertson], say goodbye and get the send-off they deserve was also special.

'We spent some amazing times together that I will cherish forever. I wish you both all the very best in your next chapters.'

#1846. New Arsenal signing sends farewell message before completing 'landmark' transfer

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Victor Ozhianvuna has bid an emotional farewell to Shamrock Rovers ahead of his move to Arsenal.

The highly-rated midfielder will head to north London after turning 18 in January, following a deal that was first agreed in October 2025.

Ozhianvuna is viewed as one of the brightest young talents in Irish football and has already made 37 senior appearances for reigning League of Ireland Premier Division champions Shamrock Rovers.

He also became the second-youngest player ever to feature in the UEFA Conference League last year.

His performances quickly caught the attention of Arsenal, who will add the Republic of Ireland Under-17 international to their academy ranks in the New Year.

Ozhianvuna - a boyhood Arsenal fan - has now said goodbye to Shamrock Rovers, where he has been since the age of six, penning a heartfelt statement on social media.

That was after a special presentation that recently took place with Ronan Finn, Shamrock Rovers’ director of football, plus their youth coach, Tony Cousins.

“After 11 amazing years, I’m saying goodbye to the club where I’ve made memories that I’ll never forget,” Ozhianvuna wrote on Instagram.

“I’ve met a lot of amazing people at the club and I’ve learned so much over the years as a footballer, but more importantly as a person and for that I’m forever grateful.

“I’d like to thank my coaches, my teammates and my friends and family for all the help over the years. I’d also like to thank the supporters for the constant love and support they’ve shown to me and to the club.

“The last few months have been difficult with an injury and I’m gutted to have not been able to play, but I couldn’t have asked for a better way to sign off than winning the league and lifting the trophy in front of the fans.

“As I move on to the next stage in my career, I’ll never forget the club that gave me a chance and I’m proud to say I’ve played for The Hoops. Forever grateful, Forever a Hoop.”

He played at the U17 World Cup in Qatar last year, but won’t be involved in this month’s tournament.

The deal to take Ozhianvuna to Arsenal is believed to be worth around £1.7million and was described at the time by Shamrock Rovers as a “landmark transfer in Irish football”.

“Delighted to have signed for this amazing club that I have supported since I was a boy,” Ozhianvuna said when his switch to Arsenal was announced. “Excited to get started.

“Thank you to everyone who has helped me get here and thank you God for everything you’ve done me.”

#1845. Chivu confident Inter can challenge in Champions League

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Cristian Chivu believes his Inter side can still compete for the Champions League this season, despite a slow start to the campaign.

After defeats to Real Madrid and Club Brugge, Inter battled to a 1-0 win over Shakhtar Donetsk last time out, though Alessandro Bastoni was sent off in the victory.

Inter have lost their last two Champions League away matches, last having a longer away losing run between October 2018 and November 2019 (four in a row).

They have also only gone 1-0 ahead in two of their last nine Champions League games, but they have gone on to win both of those, losing the other seven.

However, ahead of a trip to Feyenoord, Chivu expressed his confidence in his Inter players.

"I believe in the work, in what this team is and what it has done so far. I'm confident. They're champions, and they've shown it," Chivu said.

Next stop  Rotterdam  https://t.co/wj1WN7VZON

"There have been negative episodes and mistakes that we have to learn from, accept and move past, trying to fix them. But I’m confident.

"We've always said that the Champions League, like the league, has to be played game by game. To get into the top eight, it's around 16 points.

"For now we've won one game and lost two, but we're still in it. We know what we are and what we want, and I'm convinced we'll have a great game."

The only previous meetings between Feyenoord and Inter in the Champions League came in 2024-25, with both legs of their last 16 tie won by Inter (2-0 away and 2-1 at home).

Inter lost their first-ever game against a Dutch opponent, versus Ajax in the 1972 European Cup final. Since then, they have not lost any of their 13 matches against Dutch sides in the European Cup/Champions League, winning 10 of them (D3).

Feyenoord have lost 10 of their last 13 major European matches, but their other three games have all been home wins.
